newsitem.title: CHINA: China city builds $99 mln LPG storage facility.
newsitem.headline: China city builds $99 mln LPG storage facility.

text.p: Shantou city in China's southern Guangdong province has started building facilities for storing liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) with a total investment of $99 million, the Market Daily said on Friday.

The project, started this month and to be completed in September 1998, had been approved by the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, the newspaper said.
The facilities would include three wharfs with combined capacity of 60,000 tonnes and two underground warehouses with the ability to store 200,000 cubic metres of propane and butane, it added.

The project would be financed by $66 million in loans from the World Bank and the remaining $33 million would be jointly invested by Caltex Petroleum Corp of the United States and the Shantou Ocean Group, it said.
Caltex is a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp of the United States.
Annual LPG sales of the project were expected to reach 675,000 tonnes in 1998 and 1.905 million tonnes by 2000, it said.
